Greetings, Captain Tachenko! Glad to have you at the staging area of the 3rd Special Purpose Detachment "Osprey". This small village is our starting point. There's some chaos in the command ranks right now. Contradictory orders are coming in. Plus, there's a rumor that some convoy is heading to CNPP along the road. I hope you can bring some clarity to the situation, because the men are on edge. Especially after what they saw behind the houses near the village. You've never seen anything like it! It's like in the movies! The air swirls and distorts around a specific spot, and when one of our guys threw some gravel into it, there was a loud bang, almost like a grenade! Come on, I'll show you. If the convoy goes through, the main thing is not to run into something like that, because after the CNPP incident, there are all sorts of rumors. And we've seen all kinds of disfigured animals through binoculars... Sends shivers down your spine to see such a sight. Command said you'd have a radio through which we'll receive further orders. You've arrived, which means the order should come soon. We just need to wait.

In my humble opinion, Captain, we'll be tasked with moving ahead of the convoy, securing a key point on the route, and waiting for it there. Or maybe some reconnaissance along the route. By the way, I think since there are no order papers with you due to this mess, contacting HQ via that button in the top right corner with the hourglass icon is a good idea.

Ten seconds later, the "runner", having caught up with the squad, drops his bag with a cry: "There's ammo in there!!!" – turns, drops to one knee, and begins firing accurately at the mutants. The fighters, quickly assessing the situation, opened fire.

A Fateful Decision

After the battle, the Captain managed to speak with the fighter. He's an assistant machine gunner from Kestrel squad. The only one who survived. HQ also refused evacuation when their squad was almost entirely wiped out in an anomalous house in one of the nearby villages. After that, the squad decided to return to base on their own, but a day ago they fell into an anomaly again. Only he survived, as he was the rearguard.||A couple minutes after talking with the other guys, the newcomer pulled Tachenko aside and let him read the documents. The fighters didn't hear the conversation between the soldier and the Captain, but they saw from his face that the Commander, after reading the documents, was furious. Then they fell silent and watched what was happening. The newcomer returned to the squad, and the Captain, standing for a moment, brought the radio to his lips. The soldiers saw Tachenko's lips moving, but couldn't hear his voice due to the distance. Then the Commander lowered the radio and headed toward the fighters. Approaching the group, he threw the documents on the ground before the soldiers and said: "HQ refused evacuation. Sends us further north. I believe it's necessary to tell HQ to go to @!* and head back to the Complex. We'll hole up in the railcars there, rest, and regroup. We're on our own now. And you know, guys, I read a lot in the documents that HQ tasked us to collect. The government was doing all sorts of bad things here. And ordinary soldiers are supposed to clean it up. These snot-nosed conscripts, torn from mama's apron strings, won't clean anything up. They'll drop like flies and their families will suffer. I think only we, together with the other surviving contractors, can bring order here. We need to cleanse everything of mutants and stop this nightmare. I believe this is our DUTY".||The fighters, after a few seconds of silence, supported the Commander. No one in the squad doubted that this was truly their duty – to stop the nightmare happening here. And no one thought that in fact, Captain Tachenko, the future founder of one of the first factions in the Zone called "Duty", had not contacted HQ at all, but merely simulated the negotiations... No one knew about this for a very long time. And years later, someone in the vicinity of the Jupiter Plant, at the Cooling Towers, would find a corpse fallen from an anomaly – that of General Tachenko – with a note in his PDA about the events of the lost contact with HQ. That very loss of contact which Tachenko himself decided to make, telling no one. And only facing death did he confess, leaving a note in his PDA. It was this decision that marked the beginning of the "Fight against the Zone" by a group of people who would one day call themselves "Duty"...
